results.summary: This project is a work-in-progress design intended to drive a seven-segment display, with eight outputs mapped to the segment lines A through H. The documentation is essentially empty, consisting only of placeholders such as 'WIP' and 'TODO', so the actual functionality cannot be determined. No testing procedure or external hardware requirements are described. The design is notable only for being an incomplete template.

This project appears to be a test or placeholder design with eight inputs and eight outputs, but the documentation is largely nonsensical and incomplete. The description states 'I dont now maan!' and the test instructions say 'mayby it is broken', providing no useful information about the design's purpose or operation. External hardware is listed as 'TNT', which is not meaningful. The design cannot be evaluated from the available information.

This design implements a 2-bit adder that takes two 2-bit numbers as inputs and produces a 2-bit sum plus a carry-out. It is built from a half-adder and a full-adder, and the documentation includes a complete truth table for testing. External hardware such as switches or buttons for inputs and LEDs for outputs is recommended. The project is a straightforward educational example of binary addition.

This project is a decimal counter that counts from 0 to 9 continuously when enabled, with outputs intended for a seven-segment display. It has two inputs: one to enable counting and one to enable the decimal point. The design was not completed as planned due to personal circumstances, as noted in the documentation. Testing involves toggling the enable input and observing the display, and external hardware includes a seven-segment display and input switches.

This design is an 8-bit adder that adds corresponding bits from two 8-bit inputs, producing an 8-bit output. The documentation describes it as adding the nth and n-1th input bits to count in binary, and includes a truth table for a single-bit addition. Testing requires applying voltages to the inputs and observing the outputs, with LEDs recommended for visualization. The project is a basic educational example of binary addition.

This project implements a 1-bit full adder using NAND, XOR, and OR gates, with inputs for two operand bits and a carry-in, and outputs for sum and carry-out. Testing involves applying binary inputs and observing the outputs. No specific external hardware is required, though the documentation template suggests listing any used. The design is a fundamental building block for arithmetic circuits.

This project is a placeholder with no meaningful documentation; the title and description are incomplete or nonsensical. The pins include two inputs and one output, but the functionality is described only as 'TODO'. There is no information on how to test it or what external hardware it might need. The design cannot be assessed from the available information.

This design implements a multiplexer that selects between two inputs based on a clock signal, with the selected output on one pin and copies of the inputs on two other pins. It also includes an enable input. The documentation describes it as a workshop result and mentions a seven-segment display in the one-line description, though the display is not directly used in the described logic. Testing involves applying a clock and verifying the multiplexer behavior. External hardware is not specified.

This project is a very basic circuit that switches the output number from 0 to 1 on a seven-segment display, as described. It has two inputs and eight outputs, but the documentation states it is only for pipeline testing and advises against using it. No detailed testing procedure is provided. External hardware includes a segment display.

This project is a test design with eight inputs and eight outputs, but the documentation explicitly states that it does not work and cannot be tested. The description says 'It doesn't :3' and the test instructions say 'You can't'. No external hardware is required. The design is non-functional and serves only as a placeholder or failed experiment.
